background_notes.fact: A finite Fourier coefficient vector q on the nonzero integers has L2 norm (sum |q(k)|^2)^(1/2), equal to the supremum of |sum q(k) conjugate(z(k))| over finite z of ell2 norm at most one. For s>=0, the sequence |k|^s |hat f(k)| on k!=0 has ell2 norm at most ||f||_(H^s). For real t0 and Phi, |exp(-i t0 Phi)|=1.

background_notes.justification: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the finite pairing above by ||q||_ell2 ||z||_ell2; when q!=0 choose z=q/||q||_ell2 to attain equality, and q=0 is immediate. Since |k|<=<k> and s>=0, comparison of the squared weighted sums gives the Sobolev inequality. background_notes.fact: Mean-zero trigonometric polynomials are dense in the mean-zero subspace of H^s. L2 is complete. Consequently the polynomial trilinear estimate F002 yields, by the Cauchy construction displayed in S003, a unique continuous trilinear extension with the same bound, for each fixed admissible parameter tuple and fixed extra bounded frequency multiplier.

grounds.reason: H^s is the weighted Fourier completion of polynomials and mean zero is vanishing coefficient zero.
L2 is H^0, hence a complete Hilbert space.

background_notes.justification: Fourier truncations retain the zero coefficient and their H^s error is the tail of a convergent nonnegative weighted square sum, hence tends to zero. Given three convergent polynomial approximations, each is bounded. The trilinear telescoping identity bounds output differences by a sum with one input difference and two bounded input norms, so the outputs are Cauchy. Completeness gives the limit; the same comparison between two approximation choices proves independence. Passing the polynomial bound to the limit retains it, and passing the polynomial multilinear identities to limits gives trilinearity and continuity. Any continuous extension agrees on the dense polynomial triples and therefore everywhere. The argument is identical for each fixed multiplier and retains the common uniform constant.
